Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

MixSIARPFN 0.1.0

First release.

  • MixSIAR’s loaders, load_mix_data(), load_source_data() and load_discr_data(), with the same arguments and checks, and plot_data(). Source data can be summary statistics or raw samples (data_type = "raw", summarised to means, SDs and sample sizes).
  • run_pfn() in place of write_JAGS_model() and run_model(): marginal posteriors of every diet proportion and parameter from prior-data fitted networks, one per error structure (Residual * Process, Residual only, Process only), in about a second. Isotope data with source summary statistics (data_type = "means").
  • output_pfn() in place of output_JAGS(), with summary_table(), posterior_draws() and pfn_networks().
  • Comparison with MixSIAR: mixsiar_reference() (MixSIAR’s own fits of all nine of its isotope examples, with a posterior predictive check for killer whale, geese and wolves), mixsiar_draws(), compare_mixsiar(), plot_compare() and plot_compare_covariate().
  • Networks version 3, downloaded from Zenodo on first use and checked by SHA-256.
  • Vignettes: MixSIAR’s nine isotope examples (killer whale, geese, wolves, alligator, lake, mantis shrimp, Palmyra, snail and storm petrel), each compared with MixSIAR’s fit.
  • Article “How MixSIARPFN works and how well it does”: the network, its training, its speed, and a simulation study of 450 datasets with known diets against converged MixSIAR.
  • Article “MixSIARPFN on every simulated dataset”: all 492 simulated datasets with MixSIAR fits, including 42 benchmark designs covering the supported models.

Developed by Andrew Parnell.
